subject: Stress validation debrief & next steps for RampCo onboarding
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@rampco.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@rampco.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial load run results and a couple of anomalies

Hi Avery / Monica,

Thanks again for running the overnight stress validation. Attached is the CSV export from our load harness (rampco-load-report.csv) and a quick screenshot of the p95 tail by timestamp (latency-distribution.png). High-level notes: 

- Throughput reached the target 1.2k req/min for the steady-state window, but we saw intermittent spikes in tail latency around 03:10–03:25 PT that correlate with a model swap event.
- Error rate stayed under 0.2% except for a 7-minute blip where a 502 cascade occurred; stack trace attached in the CSV row comments.
- Memory utilization on our side climbed near 92% during the same window (DevOps logs attached).

Can your team confirm whether the model variant fallback triggered or if that aligns with known autoscaling cooldown behaviors? We'd like a concise summary of root cause and a proposed mitigation before our exec signoff on Monday.

Also, can we get the mutual action plan updated with a firm slot for a joint post-mortem? I pasted a proposed timeslot in the Drive doc.

Thanks,
Claire
Claire Huang
Head of AI Ops, RampCo

Attachments: rampco-load-report.csv, latency-distribution.png

From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@rampco.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial load run results and a couple of anomalies

Hi Claire — thanks for the artifacts and the clear summary. We pulled the run logs and here are the immediate findings: 

- The model swap you observed was a planned fallback: one replica failed a health check during the peak window and traffic shifted to the compatible quantized variant (per the route policy). That swap adds ~40–60ms p95 under sustained load; it lines up with your 03:10 window.
- The 502 cascade was from an upstream proxy that retried a timed-out request; the runtime retried once before surfacing the error. We have an internal note (ONB-512) to adjust the client retry backoff for canary traffic.
- Your memory rise looks correlated with a long-lived KV cache that wasn't evicted due to an unexpectedly long prefix in the test harness — we recommend trimming prefix size in the harness or enabling aggressive KV eviction for the next run.

Action items we propose before signoff: 
1) Redwood: produce a short artifact explaining the model-fallback timing and exact latency impact (we'll attach a 1-page PDF).
2) RampCo: run a short corrective harness (15–20 minutes) with prefix trimming to validate memory behavior.
3) Joint: 45-minute post-mortem on Thu 9am PT to agree on final acceptance evidence.

I've updated the mutual action plan in the Drive doc and attached a draft handoff note (rampco-mutual-action-plan.docx). Ben will coordinate the post-mortem invite.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Attachments: rampco-mutual-action-plan.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@rampco.com>, DevOps Team <devops@rampco.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial load run results and a couple of anomalies — scheduling post-mortem

Claire / team — I can host the post-mortem Thu 9:00–9:45am PT. Proposed agenda: 
- 9:00–9:05: quick recap of metrics and artifacts (Avery)
- 9:05–9:20: timeline & root cause hypotheses (Redwood infra + RampCo ops)
- 9:20–9:35: confirm mitigation steps & who owns each validation run
- 9:35–9:45: acceptance criteria checklist and next steps to close the benchmark gate

Pre-reads: rampco-load-report.csv, latency-distribution.png, mutual action plan (Drive link). Please attach any additional logs to ONB-512 in Jira prior to the call.

Note on acceptance criteria (draft):
- Sustained throughput: >= 1.2k req/min for a 30-minute window with 99th perc latency <= 600ms and error rate < 0.5%.
- No persistent model-fallback events during steady-state (failover allowed if hardware fault is provable).

If that checklist looks good I'll send the calendar invite and include a short runbook for the corrective harness.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@rampco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, DevOps Team <devops@rampco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial load run results and a couple of anomalies — scheduling post-mortem

Thanks Ben — Thu 9am PT works for us. We'll run the corrective harness Wed night and drop logs into ONB-512. Two quick asks before the call: 
1) Could Redwood provide the small artifact Avery mentioned (model-fallback timeline & latency delta)? We want that in the pre-read so our execs can see the tradeoff.
2) Can you confirm whether the retry backoff tweak will be a code change or a config flag? If config, we can toggle it during the Thursday run.

We'll see you on Thu.

—Claire

\n--\nThread notes: Calendar invite created for 2027-04-08T16:00:00Z (Thu 9am PT). Pre-reads uploaded to Drive. Jira ticket ONB-512 updated with the CSV and a short summary. Action owner matrix captured in Drive: Avery (artifact), Ben (runbook & invite), Claire (corrective harness), Monica (acceptance checklist).
